Anjani Sharma vs Ravindra Narayan (2024:Rj-Jd:50525) on 10
December, 2024
Author: Rekha Borana

Bench: Rekha Borana [2024:RJ-JD:50525]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Civil Transfer Appl. No. 45/2022 Anjani Sharma W/o Ravindra Narayan Sharma D/o Mojiram,
Aged About 38 Years, R/o Ward No. 22, Sardarshahar, Churu.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ----Petitioner  Versus Ravindra Narayan S/o Devnarayan Sharma, R/o Near Railway Station, Gaudhari Daa Bawri, Mandore, Jodhpur.
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Rakesh Kumar Chotia  HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE REKHA BORANA Order 10/12/2024 1.

The present transfer application has been preferred by the petitioner-Wife seeking transfer of the Divorce Petition bearing No.659/2019; Ravindra Narayan vs. Smt. Anjani Sharma filed under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 1955') by the respondent-Husband before Family Court No.3, Jodhpur (hereinafter referred to as 'Court at Jodhpur') to Additional District Judge, Churu, Camp Sardarshahar, District Churu (hereinafter referred to as 'Court at Churu').

entities.text: Ravindra Narayan vs. Smt. Anjani Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Churu, Camp Sardarshahar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The marriage between the petitioner and respondent was solemnized on 19.02.2000 as per Hindu rituals and customs.
Out of the said wedlock, two sons were born namely Bhavesh and Kabir who are 17 years and 13 years old respectively.
However, after some time, there were instances of discord and dispute between the couple.

[2024:RJ-JD:50525] (2 of 5) [CTA-45/2022]
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that because of incessant instances of cruelty and harassment by the respondent, the petitioner filed an application dated 26.11.2018 (Annexure 3) at Anjani Sharma vs Ravindra Narayan (2024:Rj-Jd:50525) on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7799238/
1 Sardarshahar under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The petitioner also lodged an FIR bearing No. 0012/2019 dated 04.01.2019 (Annexure 1) under Section 498A, IPC at Police Station Sardarshahar, District Churu of which cognizance has already been taken by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sardarshahar vide order dated 15.03.2019 (Annexure 2)
against the respondent.

Thus, the respondent- Husband only as a counterblast to the complaints filed by the petitioner-Wife and to harass her, has filed the application under Section 13 of the Act of 1955 before Court at Jodhpur.
4. Learned counsel further submits that the petitioner is residing at Sardarshahar, Churu and is financially dependent on her father for her livelihood.

The fact that she has to time and again attend court proceedings before the Court at Jodhpur which is around 400km from Sardarshahar, without any support and company of a family member, is causing her great hardship and inconvenience.
5. Although service on the sole respondent is complete, none has put in appearance.

6. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the material available on record.
7.

In view of the submissions made, this Court is of the opinion that as the petitioner-Wife is having no source of income of her own, definitely would be facing financial hardship and inconvenience as she has to travel repeatedly all by herself to [2024:RJ-JD:50525] (3 of 5) [CTA-45/2022] attend the court proceedings.
Further, other proceedings related to the same parties are admittedly pending before the Court at Churu and therefore, the present application also deserves to be transferred to the Court at Churu.

8. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha; AIR 2022 SC 4318 allowed the appeal filed by the wife for transfer of petition from Vellore to Chennai on the ground that she had to travel a long distance all by herself and also that other proceedings between the parties were already pending at Chennai.

entities.text: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha; AIR 2022 SC 4318
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court observed as under:
"9.
The cardinal principle for exercise of power Under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.

In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
Given the prevailing socio-economic paradigm in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.

10. Further, when two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, and when the decisions in the cases are interdependent, it is desirable that they [2024:RJ-JD:50525] (4 of 5) [CTA-45/2022] should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions."

Anjani Sharma vs Ravindra Narayan (2024:Rj-Jd:50525) on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7799238/
2 9.

A Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Ekta Dhadhich vs. Rajendra Prasad Sharma; S.B.
Civil Transfer Application No. 72/2021 (decided on 30.09.2021) while relying upon the judgment of Asma Praveen vs Javed Bhati; 2018 (4) RLW 3511 (Raj)

entities.text: Ekta Dhadhich vs. Rajendra Prasad Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Asma Praveen vs Javed Bhati; 2018 (4) RLW 3511 (Raj)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , observed that the comparative hardship is more to the wife and when proceedings related to same parties are pending, the Court should primarily consider the convenience of the female litigant.

The Co-ordinate Bench observed as under:
"16. It is well settled legal position that while going into the merits of a transfer application, Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants, and transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.

In such type of matters, the convenience of the wife is to be preferred over the convenience of the husband."
10.
In view of the above position of law, the present petition is allowed.
The Petition No.659/2019 pending before Family Court, No. 3, Jodhpur is directed to be transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, Churu (Camp Sardarshahar) District Churu.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Churu (Camp Sardarshahar) District Churu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
11. The Family Court No.3, Jodhpur is directed to send the complete file/record of Petition No.659/2019 (Ravindra Narayan vs. Smt. Anjani Sharma) to the Court of Additional District Judge,
[2024:RJ-JD:50525] (5 of 5) [CTA-45/2022] Churu (Camp Sardarshahar) District Churu within a period of two weeks from the receipt of the certified copy of the present order.

entities.text: Petition No.659/2019 (Ravindra Narayan vs. Smt. Anjani Sharma)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Court of Additional District Judge,
[2024:RJ-JD:50525] (5 of 5) [CTA-45/2022]
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is made clear that after the transfer of the said petition to the Court of Additional District Judge, Churu, (Camp Sardarshahar) District Churu it would proceed in accordance with law.
12. Let a certified copy of the present order be sent forthwith to Family Court No. 3, Jodhpur and Additional District Judge, Churu (Camp Sardarshahar) District Churu.
13.

entities.text: Court of Additional District Judge, Churu, (Camp Sardarshahar) District Churu
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Churu (Camp Sardarshahar) District Churu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The stay petition stands disposed of.

(REKHA BORANA),J 342-Devanshi/-
